ruling.explanation:
This ruling is addressed to both parties.

To the rider: your claim is upheld in part. The platform's GPS trace (EV-GPS-02854) measures 15.06 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff events, against a booked optimal route of 11.8 km on the trip record (EV-TRIP-02854). That is an excess of 3.26 km, or 27.63%. Under POL-RD-01 both establishment tests pass (the excess is more than 20% of the optimal distance, i.e. more than 2.36 km, and more than 0.8 km in absolute terms), so a route deviation is established on this trip's own evidence. POL-RD-01 requires me to use the trace figure (15.06 km) and not the rounded trip-record copy (15.1 km), which I have done.

To the driver: your explanation that there was a jam on the expressway is not something this ruling can act on. POL-RD-13 requires an external-traffic excuse to be tested against the traffic advisory for this trip, and the bundle holds none: EV-ADVIS-02854-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0, and its own record states no advisory covers this corridor in this window. POL-RD-03 is therefore unavailable and your assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. I record that the assertion was discarded and that no advisory was on file. Both of the traffic-excuse claims as drafted were discarded by the referee at the citation stage for failing to disclose the impaired advisory's MISSING_ARTIFACT issue code; that is a citation defect only, and the substantive position they argued is answered here anyway.

On the exculpatory routes generally: the chat log (EV-CHAT-02854) is empty (0 messages), so no rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04 exists and no distance is excluded; the trip record shows no pickup or dropoff amendment and no amended optimal distance, so POL-RD-05 cannot run; and the vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply and 11.8 km is the correct baseline.

On materiality and the driver's record: the excess (3.26 km / 27.63%) is below the POL-RD-01 materiality figures of 8.0 km and 50%, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged and no repeat-deviation pattern test runs. For completeness, the driver's citable counters (deviation_flags_90d 1 against completed_trips_90d 387) would not meet the POL-RD-06 pattern test in any event; prior_deviation_flags was mentioned by one claim but is a lifetime counter that POL-GEN-01 forbids using as a ground, and it was not used here.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02. The fare model is METERED and the surge multiplier read from the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-02854) is 1.0. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 11.8 + 0.28 x 15.9) x 1.0) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP + 0.00 surcharges + 0.00 waiting time - 0.00 promo = 17.902. charged_total is 21.45, so the refund is 21.45 - 17.902 = 3.548, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 3.55. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and well below the 90% full-refund share (it is 16.5% of the charge), so the outcome is a partial refund.

On pass-through charges: the fare breakdown carries no ERP or toll lines and no airport surcharge, so POL-RD-09 adds nothing on top of the POL-RD-02 figure, and there is no billing-integrity defect to refer. No driver compensation is due: the rider was billed for 15.1 km against a 15.06 km trace, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall.

No escalation is required. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes (100% coverage, 119 fixes at a 10 s interval, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s), so POL-RD-07(a)-(c) does not fire and no independent corroboration is needed; trip identifiers match across all three artifacts; and the refund is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling. Confidence rests on weight-1.0 artifacts, so it is not discounted. The monetary effect (3.55) is below the 8.00 execution threshold, so this provisional ruling executes automatically, subject to the appeal route under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
